title: Glover Compton in Louisville and Chicago
summary: Burton and the interviewer talk about Glover Compton, his early piano playing in Louisville houses, Paris, wife Nettie and his stroke.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: Did you know Glover Compton down in...
Glover Compton, I was just seeing him last week.
I saw him Saturday night, too.
I keep in touch with him. Yeah, I know Glover in Louisville, too.
When he first began, when he used to be a chant and billiard player, when he didn't study about piano.

He was playing piano, but he wasn't interested. He was interested in the billiard. And he was always one of my favorite piano players of that type and style that he used at that time. And the same time that Glover was playing those type of houses which they had then in Louisville, you know, well, Glover was playing at one of the houses, another fellow named Jerry was playing at another, and I was playing at a small one during that time. Because Joe Glover is not much older than I.
No, I guess that... He's... You're about 71 now.
I'm 71. Mm-hmm. And so Glover, he went to Paris and stayed over there a long while and came back.
He told us all about it. We interviewed him. We interviewed him. And his wife, too. And his wife, Nettie. Yeah, singer, of course.
Yeah, they stayed together. They made quite a feel of that entertainment. She was a great entertainer, and he was, too. And so I'm sorry to hear that he had this stroke.
Yes, he's got him all right. He's doing pretty good.
